// Package badstorefixture is a synthetic KNOWN-BAD fixture for
// qdrant_client_convergence_test.go's
// TestQdrantClientConstructedOnlyByNewQdrantClient. Scanned under the
// display path "internal/store/store.go", it proves Pitfall 5's "a second
// construction in the right FILE still trips the gate": the sanctioned
// NewQdrantClient function coexists with sneakyDial, a SECOND function in
// the same file that also constructs a client directly. Must scan with one
// sanctioned site plus exactly one violation.
//
// This file carries a .go.txt extension deliberately: it is parsed from
// source bytes by go/parser, never built by `go build`/gofmt/go vet/the
// linter, so it is not swept by any of them.
package badstorefixture

import (
	"github.com/qdrant/go-client/qdrant"
	"google.golang.org/grpc"
)

// NewQdrantClient is the one sanctioned construction site.
func NewQdrantClient(host string, port int, opts ...grpc.DialOption) (*qdrant.Client, error) {
	return qdrant.NewClient(&qdrant.Config{Host: host, Port: port, GrpcOptions: opts})
}

// sneakyDial is a second, illegitimate construction in the same file —
// isSanctionedConstruction must key on the enclosing function name, not
// merely the file path, or this bypass goes undetected.
func sneakyDial(host string, port int) (*qdrant.Client, error) {
	return qdrant.NewClient(&qdrant.Config{Host: host, Port: port})
}
